title: Chapter 9 – Competition Regulations & Tie-Breaks: Mock Exam

questions.text: What happens to results already scored against a player who withdraws having completed less than 50% of their games?

options.text: All results stand
Results are cancelled
Results are converted to half-point byes
Only wins against the withdrawn player are cancelled

questions.explanation: As per Article C05.3, if a player withdraws having completed less than 50% of their games, all results already scored against that player are cancelled. If 50% or more are completed, all results stand.

options.text: The sum of a player's own scores across all rounds
The sum of the final scores of all of a player's opponents
The number of wins minus the number of losses
The average rating of all opponents faced

questions.explanation: As per Article C07.2, the Buchholz score is the sum of the final scores of all of a player's opponents. A higher Buchholz score indicates the player faced stronger opposition.

questions.text: The Sonneborn-Berger system is used primarily in which type of tournament?

options.text: Swiss System tournaments
Knock-out tournaments
Round Robin tournaments
Scheveningen System tournaments

questions.explanation: As per Article C07.3, the Sonneborn-Berger score is used primarily in Round Robin tournaments. It rewards winning against stronger opponents more than winning against weaker ones.

questions.text: How far in advance must an international tournament be publicly announced?

options.text: At least 15 days
At least 30 days
At least 60 days
At least 90 days

questions.explanation: As per Article C05.2, international tournaments must be announced publicly at least 60 days before the start. National events require at least 30 days. The announcement must include all key details.

questions.text: When must the tie-break system be announced in a tournament?

options.text: After the final round when ties are known
Before the start of the tournament
At the start of the final round
Only if a tie actually occurs

questions.explanation: As per Article C07.1, the tie-break system to be used must be announced before the start of the tournament. This ensures all participants know the rules before they begin competing.

questions.text: What is the Median Buchholz (also called Cut Buchholz)?

options.text: The Buchholz score with the highest opponent's score added
The Buchholz score with the lowest and/or highest opponent scores removed
The median of all players' Buchholz scores in the event
The Buchholz score calculated only for the middle rounds

questions.explanation: Per Article C07.2, Median (Cut) Buchholz removes the lowest and/or highest opponents' scores from the standard Buchholz calculation. This reduces the impact of an exceptionally weak or strong single opponent.

questions.text: What happens when two players have the same score and all tie-break criteria are equal?

options.text: They share the prize money equally
An Armageddon game or play-off is mandatory
The higher-rated player is ranked above the lower-rated player
Lots are drawn to determine final ranking

questions.explanation: Per Article C07.4, when all tie-break criteria result in equality, players share the prize money and/or title equally. A play-off is only required if a title or medal (not shared prize money) must be awarded to a single player.

questions.text: What is the Sonneborn-Berger score calculation?

options.text: Sum of the final scores of all opponents
Sum of the scores of opponents beaten, plus half the scores of opponents drawn against
Sum of the final scores of all opponents multiplied by game result
Number of wins divided by number of games played

questions.explanation: Per Article C07.3, the Sonneborn-Berger score = (sum of the final scores of each player beaten) + (sum of half the final scores of each player drawn against). Losses contribute 0. It measures the quality of results.

questions.text: How is the drawing of lots used in a tournament?

options.text: To decide who wins when all tiebreaks are equal
To determine starting order, player numbers and colour for first round
To select which games are broadcast live
To randomly reduce the number of players in large events

questions.explanation: Per Article C05.4, drawing of lots is used at the start of a tournament to determine the player numbers (starting order) and, in Round Robin events, the order of players which determines their first-round pairings and colours.

questions.text: Who comprises an appeals committee in a FIDE event?

options.text: The Chief Arbiter and two senior arbiters
Representatives of the players or their captains only
A committee independent of the arbiters, usually nominated by the players or federations
FIDE headquarters appoints the committee remotely

questions.explanation: Per Article C06.2, the appeals committee must be independent of the arbiters. It is typically composed of representatives nominated by the participating players or federations, or persons appointed by the organiser before the event.
